mentions.name: This and That
mentions.description: A tool that makes unstructured operating knowledge maintain itself by automatically updating customer pages. It captures valuable customer insights — like plans to open new locations — that currently live in email, Slack threads, internal discussions and meeting transcripts, and writes them back to the customer record so everyone who talks to that customer is up to date. The team is currently working on the cold-start problem: figuring out which entity types (customers, competitors, products) a company cares about and building those lists without handing them a manual setup task.
mentions.problem: Valuable unstructured customer knowledge is buried in email, Slack and meeting transcripts, and nobody updates the customer page because the payoff is deferred — so there is often no good place to store that information and teammates miss it.
mentions.audience: Salespeople and anyone on the team who talks to customers
mentions.source_excerpt:
I'm working on making unstructured operating knowledge maintain itself. If a customer's phone number changes, that goes in the CRM. But if a salesperson learns the customer is planning to open new locations, everyone else who talks to that customer should know, and today they mostly don't. In fact, there's probably not even a good place for that valuable nugget to be stored.

The information exists. It's in email and Slack, in threads with the customer, internal discussions, meeting transcripts. But nobody updates the customer page since the payoff is deferred. We're trying to update it automatically.
mentions.author: jreynar
